For a soy sauce substitute that maintains the savory, umami profile of a stir-fry while being soy-free, coconut aminos are the best option. They have a similar consistency and saltiness but are slightly sweeter and milder. Another good alternative is tamari if the allergy is strictly to soy protein but not gluten, though many soy-allergic individuals also react to tamari, so coconut aminos are safer. You can also use a mixture of beef or mushroom broth with a splash of vinegar and a pinch of salt to mimic the depth of flavor.
